---
title: "User costs over the last 90 days"
subtitle: "NASA Openscapes hub"
date: today
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
devtools::load_all(here::here(), quiet = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)

set_env_vars("nasa")

end_date <- Sys.Date()
start_date <- end_date - 90

daily <- get_daily_user_costs(start_date = start_date, end_date = end_date)

per_user <- daily |>
  dplyr::summarise(cost = sum(cost), .by = c(user, component)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = component,
    values_from = cost,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = compute + `home storage`) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-user, names_to = "component", values_to = "cost") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c("compute", "home storage", "total"),
      labels = c("Compute", "Home storage", "Overall")
    )
  )

with_cost <- dplyr::filter(per_user, cost > 0)

dollar <- scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 0.01)
hubs <- sort(unique(daily$hub))
```

Per-user compute and home storage costs on the `{r} knitr::combine_words(hubs)`
hubs, `{r} format(start_date, "%B %e")` to `{r} format(end_date - 1, "%B %e, %Y")`.
Shared costs (core nodes, networking, object storage) are not included.

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Cost per user over 90 days. Statistics are over users with a cost greater than zero for that component."
with_cost |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Users = dplyr::n(),
    Total = sum(cost),
    Min = min(cost),
    Median = stats::median(cost),
    Mean = mean(cost),
    Max = max(cost),
    .by = component
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(component) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(Total:Max, dollar)) |>
  dplyr::rename(Component = component) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrrr")
```

## Distribution

```{r}
#| label: fig-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Cost per user over 90 days. Each dot is one user."
#| fig-alt: "Three strips of dots, one each for compute, home storage and overall, showing each user's 90-day cost on a log scale from under one cent to several hundred dollars. Most users cost under a few dollars, and a small number of users, mostly in compute, cost tens to hundreds of dollars."
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 8
plot_data <- dplyr::mutate(
  with_cost,
  component = factor(component, levels = rev(levels(component)))
)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = cost, y = component)) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(height = 0.2, width = 0, seed = 1),
    size = 1.6,
    alpha = 0.5,
    colour = "#2a6fdb"
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 0.01)) +
  labs(x = "Cost per user (USD, log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

## Highest-cost users

```{r}
#| label: tbl-top-users
#| tbl-cap: "The 10 users with the highest total cost over 90 days."
per_user |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = cost) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(Overall, n = 10) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-user, dollar)) |>
  dplyr::rename(User = user) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrr")
```
